findings.category: OWASP A08 Software and Data Integrity Failures
findings.title: Unsafe deserialization via pickle.load on model and SHAP artifacts
findings.description: The pipeline uses Python pickle deserialization on files under config-controlled directories (models_dir and results_dir/shap). Pickle is code-execution by design. If an attacker can get a crafted .pkl into those directories or convince a user to run the CLI against attacker-provided artifacts/config, this becomes arbitrary code execution in the user's environment.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Attacker prepares a malicious pickle payload (uses __reduce__ to run a command). 2) Attacker supplies a config YAML with models_dir/results_dir pointing at attacker-controlled directories and a matching malicious file like rf_fold_0.pkl or shap/*_full.pkl. 3) Victim runs: python -m src.main --config /path/to/attacker.yaml --skip-train. 4) Code reaches pickle.load(...) and executes attacker-controlled code.
findings.impact: Arbitrary code execution as the user running the pipeline (credential theft, data exfiltration, lateral movement on shared machines).
findings.recommendation: Eliminate pickle for SHAP payloads (use npz + JSON), and use a safer sklearn serialization format (e.g., skops) for trained models. At minimum, require integrity verification (signed artifacts) before loading any pickle.
